title: Running a civil recovery suit alongside a cheque bounce case
p1:
A cheque bounces. Can you pursue the money through a civil court while also filing a cheque bounce case?

Yes. And this is something many creditors don't realise when someone defaults on a payment.
p2:
There is a common misconception that choosing one legal route means giving up the other.

In India, a cheque bounce case under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and a civil recovery suit serve different purposes.

The cheque bounce case addresses the legal consequences of issuing a cheque that is dishonoured. The civil suit focuses on recovering the actual outstanding amount.
p3:
Here's the practical insight: You generally don't have to wait for the cheque bounce proceedings to finish before initiating a civil recovery action.

Both proceedings can run simultaneously, subject to applicable legal requirements.

However, you cannot recover the same debt twice. Any amount received through one proceeding must be properly accounted for in the other.

Keep the cheque, bank return memo, invoices, payment records, agreements and legal notices safely documented. These can strengthen your recovery strategy.

The key is to pursue both remedies strategically, not treat them as two separate opportunities to collect the same money.
conclusion: If someone owes you money and their cheque bounces, would you pursue both legal remedies simultaneously or wait for the cheque bounce case to conclude? What would influence your decision?
